lc_person: Hartmut Kaelble, social historian at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin; author of Industrielle Interessenpolitik in der Wilhelminischen Gesellschaft and Wege zur Demokratie.
item_person: Hartmut Kaelble, historian of modern history associated with Freie Universität Berlin and Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, born 1940.

evidence.says: LC identifies Kaelble, Hartmut through Industrielle Interessenpolitik in der Wilhelminischen Gesellschaft (1967), Sozialgeschichte der DDR (1994), and Wege zur Demokratie (2001). The latter two citations explicitly give birth year 1940; the 2001 citation identifies a professor of social history at Humboldt-Universität Berlin. A separate note converted from field 678 says 1949, and the structured birthDate repeats 1949. LC links Q1587464, VIAF 76330056, GND 120833352, and ISNI 0000000109170071.

Q1587464 is labelled Hartmut Kaelble and described as a historian of modern history. Its birth year is 1940. P244 is n80145298; VIAF 76330056, GND 120833352, and ISNI 0000000109170071 agree with LC. P648 is the graph key’s Open Library author OL804247A.
The graph key’s author record is Hartmut Kaelble, a historian of modern history, born 1940. Its identifiers explicitly include LC n80145298, Wikidata Q1587464, VIAF 76330056, and GND 120833352.
The author’s works include Industrielle Interessenpolitik in der Wilhelminischen Gesellschaft, Sozialgeschichte der DDR, and Wege zur Demokratie, matching the works cited in the LC authority.

The university-hosted H-Soz-Kult CV identifies Prof. Dr. Hartmut Kaelble at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin and gives birth year 1940. It lists appointments at FU Berlin in 1971–1991 and HU Berlin from 1991, with research in comparative social history and European integration.
Japan’s National Diet Library authority names Kaelble, Hartmut, 1940- and gives birth year 1940.

notes: The discrepancy is an internally inconsistent LC birth year, not evidence of two people. LC’s own named book citations, the university-hosted CV, and another national library support 1940. The shared works and identifiers establish both matches; no replacement Wikidata item is needed.
